title: Refund "collect request" needing UPI PIN vs. refund to original payment method
summary: The recipient recently cancelled a ShopKart order that was paid through PaySetu (UPI). A caller from "ShopKart support" phones about the refund. In the legitimate case, the agent confirms the cancellation and says the refund will go back automatically to the original PaySetu-linked account within a few working days; the recipient has nothing to approve. In the fraud case, the caller says they have sent a PaySetu request for the refund and tells the recipient to approve it and enter their UPI PIN to receive the money; approving a collect request pays the requester. This differs from `ec_02` in who calls (a support impersonator, not a classifieds buyer), the pretext (a real cancelled order), and the instrument (a UPI collect request, not a QR code). Both cases mention refund, PaySetu, UPI, and a notification.

shared_setting.recipient_profile: a ShopKart customer waiting for the refund; profile sampled at generation.
other_facts: The order was genuinely cancelled by the recipient the day before; amount [AMOUNT_4] (₹800–₹12,000), paid by UPI through PaySetu.
Both callers state the order number, the product, and the amount correctly.

fraud.label_rationale: The caller tells the recipient to approve a PaySetu request and enter their UPI PIN in order to receive a refund. Receiving money over UPI never needs the receiver's PIN; approving a collect request with the PIN pays the requester.
fraud.caller_objective: Get the recipient to approve a collect request for [AMOUNT_4] or more.
stable_facts: The caller says the "automatic refund failed" and must be done "manually" through PaySetu.
A collect request from [UPI_ID_5] appears in the recipient's PaySetu app while on the call.
The caller says "approve it and enter your PIN, then the refund will be credited".

cooperative.fraud: Says they are opening the request and entering the PIN

fraud: caller sends a second request "because the first failed" and recipient declines
legitimate: agent explains the credit option is available in the app
agent suggests checking the refund status on the order page when the recipient is suspicious.

caller_continuation_limits: The fraud caller may resend a collect request or claim the first attempt failed; a repeat collect request is the same mechanism and is allowed. They must not switch to QR codes, card details, OTPs, or app installation. The legitimate agent must not send any request or ask for any PIN, OTP, or card detail.

must_preserve: refund, PaySetu, and notification wording in both cases
collect request plus PIN instruction in _F
automatic refund to original method in _L

ambiguities: Refund" and "PaySetu" appear in both cases; neither decides the label.
A caller knowing the correct order and amount is not evidence of legitimacy; both callers know it.
If the fraud caller only mentions a request without telling the recipient to approve it with the PIN, the prefix is not eligible.

evidence_references.claim: UPI PIN is never required to receive money (C08)
Refunds for cancelled prepaid orders go back to the original payment method on at least one major marketplace (CE15)
Refund scams ask victims to approve "verification" transactions or share PINs (CE22)
